questions.topic: Optimization — restrict Qualifier and Pointer Aliasing
questions.q: What does the `restrict` keyword guarantee to the compiler when optimizing this loop?
questions.hint: Think about whether writing to address `a[i]` can change the value read from `b[i]`.
options: Pointers `a` and `b` refer to non-overlapping memory regions, enabling vector optimization without unnecessary reloads from RAM
Arrays `a` and `b` have strictly the same physical size `n`
Elements of arrays `a` and `b` are forbidden from being modified inside the loop
explanations: Correct! The `restrict` qualifier (C99) informs the compiler that access to the object in this scope is achieved exclusively through this pointer. This guarantees no memory aliasing and enables SIMD vector optimization.
Incorrect. Array size is passed via a separate variable `n`; `restrict` does not check sizes.
Incorrect. Prohibition of modification is specified by the `const` keyword, not `restrict`.

questions.topic: C99 Standards — Compound Literals in Loops
questions.q: What value will `printf` output when using compound literal `((int[]){10, 20, 30})[i]` inside a loop?
questions.hint: What storage duration does a compound literal declared inside a loop body have?
options: Undefined Behavior (UB)
explanations: Incorrect. The loop will sum all 3 elements of the compound literal.
Incorrect. This is the value of only the last element `[2]`.

Correct! In C99, a compound literal inside a block has automatic storage duration of the current block. On each iteration, array `{10, 20, 30}` is created, element `[i]` is read, and summation occurs: 10 + 20 + 30 = 60.
Incorrect. Array elements are initialized with values 10, 20, and 30.
Incorrect. Literal memory is valid throughout the current iteration of the block.

questions.topic: C Standards — Attempting to Modify an Originally const Object
questions.q: What is the status of code execution when casting away the `const` qualifier via explicit `(int *)&val`?
questions.hint: Distinguish between a pointer to a constant and an object ORIGINALLY declared as `const`.
options: Outputs 20
Outputs 10
Undefined Behavior
Compilation error
explanations: Incorrect. Although type casting suppresses the compiler warning, performing such an operation is forbidden by the standard.
Incorrect. The compiler may place a `const` variable in read-only memory section (e.g. `.rodata`).

Correct! According to ISO C, attempting to modify an object originally declared with a `const` qualifier through a non-const pointer leads to Undefined Behavior (UB). Code may crash with a Segmentation Fault.
Incorrect. Explicit type cast `(int *)&val` forces compiler to process code without errors.

questions.topic: Type Conversions — Integer Promotions
questions.q: Will unsigned overflow occur in addition `(a + b)` for type `unsigned short`?
questions.hint: Recall to what type types smaller than `int` are automatically promoted when participating in arithmetic operations.
options: Promotion to `signed int` will cause expression `(65535 + 1)` to evaluate to 65536, condition is true (`65536 > 0`), `count` becomes 1
Addition `a + b` will overflow modulo in `unsigned short` (value 0), condition is false (`0 > 0`), `count` remains 0
explanations: Correct! Under Integer Promotions, if `int` can hold all values of the original type (and 32-bit `int` holds 65535 of `unsigned short`), operands are automatically promoted to `signed int`. Result $65535 + 1 = 65536 > 0$ (true).
Incorrect. Addition does NOT happen in type `unsigned short`, because it is first promoted to `int`.

questions.topic: Low-Level Jumps — setjmp/longjmp and volatile Variables
questions.q: Why is variable `count` declared with `volatile` specifier when working with `setjmp` and `longjmp`?
questions.hint: What happens to local variables stored in CPU registers upon calling `longjmp`?
options: To preserve variable modifications: values of non-volatile local variables modified between `setjmp` and `longjmp` become indeterminate
To guarantee atomicity of operations on `count` during jump
To allow calling `longjmp` from other threads of execution
This is optional, variable will be preserved without `volatile` as well
explanations: Correct! ISO C standard explicitly states: if a local automatic variable is modified between `setjmp` and `longjmp` and is NOT declared `volatile`, its value after `longjmp` is indeterminate (since compiler could store it in a register restored from `jmp_buf`).
Incorrect. `volatile` is unrelated to operation atomicity.
Incorrect. `setjmp/longjmp` in C were not intended for multithreaded synchronization.
Incorrect. Without `volatile`, an optimizing compiler will 'roll back' `count` value to 0.

questions.topic: Structures — Signed Bit-Fields and Their Limits
questions.q: What value will signed bit-field `signed int x : 2` of 2 bits width take after iterations?
questions.hint: Range of a signed 2-bit field in two's complement is from -2 to +1.
options: Range of 2-bit signed field is -2 to 1; signed bit-field overflow result is implementation-defined / UB
Field overflows through chain of values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
Field will retain value 5
Compilation error due to using `++` operator on a bit-field
Field will equal 1, and `count` will equal 5
Field will equal 0, and `count` will equal 5
explanations: Correct! Bit-field `signed int x : 2` stores signed values [-2, 1]. On `0 + 1` we get 1. Upon next increment, signed bit-field overflow in C is Implementation-Defined / UB. Usually resets to -2.
Incorrect. Two signed bits cannot represent positive numbers 2, 3, or 4.
Incorrect. Value 5 requires at least 4 bits (for signed representation).
Incorrect. Increment operators `++` are syntactically permitted for bit-fields in C.
Incorrect. Value will not stop at 1 due to continuing loop.
Incorrect. Depending on platform, value will cycle within 2-bit range.

questions.topic: Scope — Triple Variable Shadowing
questions.q: What will `printf("%d", i)` output after given `for` loop completes?
questions.hint: In C99, `for(int i...)` header creates a separate scope block, and body `{ int i... }` creates its own nested block.
options: Compilation error
explanations: Correct! There are 3 different variables `i` here: 1) Outer `i = 100`. 2) Loop variable `for (int i = 0)`. 3) Inner `int i = 10` in loop body block. Inner modifies to 11 and is destroyed. Loop counter reaches 3 and is destroyed. Outer `i = 100` remains intact.
Incorrect. Loop variable `i`, which became 3, ceases to exist upon loop exit.
Incorrect. Re-declaring a variable with same name IN INNER block is completely valid.

questions.topic: Pointer Types — Prohibition of void* Arithmetic in ISO C
questions.q: Why does offsetting `ptr` in strict ISO C standard require explicit cast `(char *)ptr + 1`?
questions.hint: What is `sizeof(void)` equal to in pure C language standard?
options: In ISO C, arithmetic on `void*` is forbidden because `void` is an incomplete type without size (`sizeof(void)` is undefined)
Type `void*` is automatically converted only during pointer subtraction
Without `(char*)` cast, `void*` offset will automatically step by 4 bytes
Type `void*` in C is a constant pointer by default
explanations: Correct! Under ISO C standard, type `void` is an incomplete type, and `sizeof(void)` has no value. Therefore `ptr + 1` is syntactically invalid in pure C (though GCC compiler has an extension where `sizeof(void) == 1`).
Incorrect. Arithmetic is forbidden for all addition and subtraction operations with `void*` equally.
Incorrect. Standard does not equate `void*` to `int*` (4 bytes).
Incorrect. Mutability of pointer is determined by `const` qualifier, not `void` type.

questions.topic: sizeof Operator — Expression Evaluation Exceptions (VLA Evaluation)
questions.q: Will side effect `i++` evaluate inside `sizeof(int[i++])`?
questions.hint: Are expressions inside `sizeof` evaluated if operand is a VLA (Variable Length Array)?
options: Yes! Starting with C99, if `sizeof` operand is a VLA, expression is evaluated at Runtime
No, `sizeof` operand is always a compile-time unevaluated operand
Compilation error
Undefined Behavior (UB)
explanations: Correct! This is a unique exception of C99+ standards: if `sizeof` operand type is a VLA (Variable Length Array), array size is unknown at compile time, so expression INSIDE `sizeof` is evaluated at runtime, and increment `i++` triggers!
Incorrect. This rule holds for all regular types, but NOT for VLA types.
Incorrect. VLA syntax inside `sizeof` is completely correct in C99.
Incorrect. Behavior is strictly defined by standard.

questions.topic: C99 Standards — Flexible Array Member
questions.q: What rule of C99 standard describes flexible array member `int data[]` in a structure?
questions.hint: Where exactly inside a structure must a flexible array member be located, and is it included in `sizeof` of the structure?
options: Flexible array member must be the LAST element of structure, and `sizeof(struct Buffer)` does NOT include memory for `data[]` elements
Size `sizeof(struct Buffer)` automatically includes default size of 1 element
Elements `data[]` are automatically allocated on stack upon structure declaration
explanations: Correct! In C99, Flexible Array Member (`type name[]`) must strictly be the last field of structure. When computing `sizeof(struct)`, memory for this array is not included; it is allocated dynamically via `malloc(sizeof(struct) + N * sizeof(elem))`.
Incorrect. Unlike obsolete trick with `data[1]`, `data[]` adds no bytes to structure size.
Incorrect. Memory for flexible array must be explicitly allocated in dynamic memory (heap).

questions.topic: Multidimensional VLAs — 2D Variable Length Arrays in Loops
questions.q: What will sum of all elements of 2D VLA array `arr[2][3]` equal?
questions.hint: Iterations $i=0, j \in [0..2]$ add $(0+0)+(0+1)+(0+2) = 3$. Calculate $i=1$.
explanations: Correct! At `i=0`: elements 0, 1, 2 (sum 3). At `i=1`: elements 1, 2, 3 (sum 6). Total sum of all elements of VLA array equals $3 + 6 = 9$.
Incorrect. Elements of row `i=0` forgotten.
Incorrect. Re-check index sums for last row.
Incorrect. Variable `sum` accumulates results in loop.

questions.topic: C11 Standards — Memory Alignment via aligned_alloc
questions.q: What strict requirement does function `aligned_alloc(alignment, size)` from C11 standard impose on size parameter `size`?
questions.hint: Can `size` be smaller or not a multiple of alignment value `alignment`?
options: Parameter `size` must strictly be a multiple of alignment value `alignment`
Alignment `alignment` must necessarily be an odd number
Size `size` must equal exactly 1024 bytes
Function `aligned_alloc` allocates memory exclusively on stack
explanations: Correct! In C11 standard for `aligned_alloc(alignment, size)`, parameter `size` MUST be a multiple of `alignment` (in example `64` is multiple of `64`). Otherwise function returns `NULL` or triggers UB.
Incorrect. Alignment in C must always be a power of two.
Incorrect. Fixed restriction of 1024 bytes does not exist.
Incorrect. Function `aligned_alloc` allocates memory on heap, similarly to `malloc`.

questions.topic: C Standards — Strict Aliasing Rule
questions.q: What key C language rule is violated when writing to memory of float variable via `int *p = (int *)&f`?
questions.hint: Does standard allow reading and writing memory of one type via pointer to an incompatible type?
options: Strict Aliasing Rule — accessing a `float` object via `int*` pointer causes UB
Alignment Rule
Lifetime Rule of global variables
`const` Type Casting Rule
C syntax error
explanations: Correct! Strict Aliasing Rule forbids accessing memory of one type via pointer to another incompatible type (except `char*`). Compiler assumes `f` and `*p` are distinct objects, and may omit writes from loop during optimization.
Incorrect. `int` and `float` usually have same alignment (4 bytes).
Incorrect. Variable is on stack, its lifetime is valid.
Incorrect. Qualifier `const` is not used here.
Incorrect. Code compiles successfully, but contains logical standard UB.

questions.topic: Dynamic Memory — 2D Arrays via Pointer to Pointer
questions.q: What will element `matrix[1][0]` equal after initializing dynamic matrix in loop?
questions.hint: Substitute indices `i = 1` and `j = 0` into formula `i + j + 1`.
explanations: Correct! At `i = 1` and `j = 0`, formula calculation gives: $1 + 0 + 1 = 2$. Value of `matrix[1][0]` becomes 2.
Incorrect. 1 is obtained for element `matrix[0][0]`.
Incorrect. 3 is obtained for element `matrix[1][1]`.

questions.topic: Aliasing Exceptions — Memory Inspection via char* / unsigned char*
questions.q: Why does this Endianness detection code via `unsigned char*` NOT violate Strict Aliasing?
questions.hint: Which data types in C standard are officially allowed to alias memory of absolutely ANY object?
options: Character types (`char`, `unsigned char`, `signed char`) are official exceptions in C standards for byte-by-byte memory inspection of any object
Because type `unsigned int` is automatically cast to array upon reading
Violates, this code causes Undefined Behavior (UB)
Due to writing numbers in hexadecimal notation `0x`
explanations: Correct! ISO C standard explicitly makes an exception from Strict Aliasing rules for types `char`, `signed char`, and `unsigned char`. Pointers to character types are permitted to read and inspect memory representation of any other object.
Incorrect. Automatic conversion to array does not happen.
Incorrect. Code is standardized and is a classic way to test Little/Big Endian.
Incorrect. Hexadecimal number notation (`0x`) in no way affects compiler aliasing rules.

questions.topic: Arrays and Pointers — Subscript Operator Symmetry
questions.q: Is `2[arr]` syntax valid in C, and what will this line output?
questions.hint: Recall what expression `a[b]` expands to at pointer level.
options: Compilation error
Undefined behavior
explanations: Correct! In C, expression `a[b]` is by definition equivalent to `*(a + b)`. Due to commutativity of addition, `*(a + b)` equals `*(b + a)`. Therefore `2[arr]` is strictly equivalent to `arr[2]` and returns third element (30).
Incorrect. Such syntax fully conforms to ANSI/ISO C standard.
Incorrect. 10 is `arr[0]` or `0[arr]`.
Incorrect. Operation is strictly defined by standard.

questions.topic: Arrays — Exceptions to Pointer Decay Rule
questions.q: What will `printf("%zu %zu", sizeof(arr), sizeof(arr + 0))` output on 64-bit architecture?
questions.hint: The `sizeof` operator is one of rare exceptions where array name does NOT automatically decay to a pointer.
explanations: Correct! Operator `sizeof(arr)` takes array itself as operand and returns its full size in bytes ($5 \times 4 = 20$). Expression `arr + 0` causes explicit pointer addition, causing `arr` to decay to `int*`. Size of a pointer on 64-bit system is 8 bytes. Output: 20 8.
Incorrect. In `sizeof(arr + 0)`, operand is result of pointer addition, not array itself.
Incorrect. `sizeof(arr)` returns memory size of entire array, not pointer size.
Incorrect. `sizeof` returns size in bytes, not element count.

questions.topic: Strings — Modifying String Literals
questions.q: What effect will attempting to write `s[0] = 'h'` to a pointer to string literal lead to?
questions.hint: In which memory region does compiler usually place string literals?
options: Undefined Behavior (UB) / Segmentation Fault
Successfully modifies string to "hello"
Compilation error
String becomes empty
explanations: Correct! Under ISO C standard, string literals are immutable (read-only) and are often placed in protected memory sections (e.g. `.rodata`). Attempting to write to `s[0]` triggers Undefined Behavior (UB), leading to Segmentation Fault.
Incorrect. Only character arrays (`char s[] = "Hello"`) can be modified, not literals via `char*`.
Incorrect. In C (unlike C++), type of string literal is `char[]`, not `const char[]`, so code compiles without error.
Incorrect. Modification causes program crash, not clearing.

questions.topic: Pointers — Pointer Arithmetic on Array Pointers int (*p)[N]
questions.q: What does `(*p)[0]` equal after incrementing pointer `p` to array of 3 elements?
questions.hint: Pointer `p` has type `int (*)[3]`. How many bytes will `p` shift by when executing `p++`?
options: Compilation error
explanations: Correct! `p` is a pointer to an ARRAY of 3 `int` elements (`sizeof(int[3]) = 12` bytes). Increment `p++` shifts pointer forward by a whole row of 3 elements. `*p` now refers to second row `{4, 5, 6}`, and `(*p)[0]` returns first element of this row — 4.
Incorrect. 2 is second element of first row `arr[0][1]`.
Incorrect. 1 is first element of first row prior to increment.
Incorrect. Declaration of pointer to array `int (*p)[3]` is syntactically correct.

questions.topic: C99 Standards — Designated Initializers
questions.q: What will sum of elements of array `int arr[5] = {[1] = 10, [3] = 20}` equal?
questions.hint: What happens to array elements whose indices are not specified during explicit initialization?
options: Indeterminate value (garbage from memory)
explanations: Correct! In C99 designated initializers allow explicitly setting element values `arr[1] = 10` and `arr[3] = 20`. According to C standard, if an array is partially initialized, all uninitialized elements are automatically zero-filled. Array looks like `{0, 10, 0, 20, 0}`. Sum: 30.
Incorrect. Do not forget accounted value `arr[3] = 20`.
Incorrect. Do not forget accounted value `arr[1] = 10`.
Incorrect. Garbage remains only if initializers are COMPLETELY absent (`int arr[5];`).

questions.topic: Data Types — Incompatibility of int** and 2D Array int[][N]
questions.q: Why does passing 2D array `int arr[2][2]` to a function with `int **p` parameter without casting cause UB when accessing `p[0][0]`?
questions.hint: Is a 2D array an array of pointers or a continuous matrix of numbers?
options: 2D array is a continuous block of data. Expression `p[0]` reads first 4/8 bytes of array and interprets numerical element value itself as ADDRESS in memory
Because 2D arrays are passed by value, not by reference
Because `int**` allocates memory on stack, while `arr[2][2]` on heap
This is a completely safe operation in C11
explanations: Correct! In memory `arr[2][2]` is simply 4 consecutive `int` numbers. Parameter `int **p` expects a POINTER `int*` to lie at address `p`. Attempting to dereference `p[0]` forces processor to take numerical value of `arr[0][0]` (e.g., 1) and access memory at address `0x1`, causing crash.
Incorrect. Arrays in C are never passed by value.
Incorrect. Local arrays are declared on stack.
Incorrect. This is a severe pointer type bug.

questions.topic: Strings — Embedded Null Terminators and string.h Functions
questions.q: What will `printf` output for string with embedded null terminators `"A\0B\0C"`?
questions.hint: Think about how `sizeof` determines string literal size and how `strlen` finds end of string.
explanations: Correct! `sizeof(str)` counts total array memory including literal trailing `\0`: 'A', '\0', 'B', '\0', 'C', '\0' = 6 bytes. Function `strlen(str)` searches for first encountered null byte `\0` immediately following 'A', so length equals 1. Output: 6 1.
Incorrect. `strlen` does not count characters after first encountered `\0`.
Incorrect. Automatic trailing null terminator of literal itself forgotten.
Incorrect. Null bytes in middle of array are ignored.

questions.topic: Strings — Missing Null Terminator
questions.q: What will happen when passing array `char str[3] = {'a', 'b', 'c'}` to `%s` specifier of `printf`?
questions.hint: How does `printf` determine where printed string ends?
options: Out-of-bounds read and Undefined Behavior (UB) will occur
Prints "abc"
Compilation error
Prints "abc\0"
explanations: Correct! 3-element array is filled with characters without `\0` byte. Specifier `%s` expects null-terminated string. `printf` will read memory past array bounds until it hits arbitrary 0 in memory (UB).
Incorrect. Without `\0`, output will guaranteed continue with memory garbage.
Incorrect. Initializing character array without `\0` is syntactically legal.
Incorrect. Symbol `\0` itself is not printed.

questions.topic: Pointers and Arrays — Flat Linear Indexing of Multidimensional Array
questions.q: What will `*p` equal if 2D array `a[3][3]` is cast to `int*` and 4 is added?
questions.hint: Array elements lie sequentially in memory. Which element by count will be at offset 4?
options: Undefined behavior
explanations: Correct! 2D array is stored sequentially in memory (Row-Major Order): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Casting to `(int*)a` gives address of first element (1). Offset `+ 4` points to 5th element (index 4), which equals 5.
Incorrect. 4 is element with index 3.
Incorrect. 6 is element with index 5.
Incorrect. Traversal over continuous array via base pointer is standardized.

questions.topic: C99 Standards — Lifetime of VLA Array Inside Loops
questions.q: What happens to memory of VLA (Variable Length Array) created inside `for` loop body on each iteration?
questions.hint: How does block scope affect allocation and deallocation of VLA memory on stack?
options: VLA memory is allocated on stack upon entry into loop block and automatically deallocated upon each exit from iteration block
Memory is allocated on heap and accumulates until end of function, creating memory leak
Memory is allocated once before loop start and reused
Creating VLAs inside loops is forbidden
explanations: Correct! In C99 VLA lifetime is bound to its block scope. On each iteration of loop upon entering block, stack frame is allocated for VLA, and upon exiting block (reaching `}` or `continue`), automatic VLA memory is immediately cleared.
Incorrect. VLAs are placed on stack, not on heap.
Incorrect. Since size can change each iteration, allocation happens anew.
Incorrect. Declaring VLA inside loop blocks is completely permitted.

questions.topic: Pointers — Negative Indices in Pointers
questions.q: Is expression `p[-1]` legal in C if `p` points to `&arr[2]`?
questions.hint: What does `p[-1]` expand to according to pointer arithmetic rules?
options: Yes, completely legal, outputs 20
No, negative indices are forbidden by C syntax
Causes Undefined Behavior (UB)
Outputs 10
explanations: Correct! Expression `p[-1]` turns into `*(p - 1)`. Since `p` points to `arr[2]` (value 30), `p - 1` points to `arr[1]` (value 20). Since this element is within original array bounds, operation is completely legal.
Incorrect. Unlike other languages, C allows using negative indices for pointers.
Incorrect. UB occurs only if dereferenced address exceeds array bounds.
Incorrect. 10 is `arr[0]` or `p[-2]`.

questions.topic: Preprocessor / Lexing — Automatic String Literal Concatenation
questions.q: What is `sizeof(str)` equal to for expression `"Hello " "World"`?
questions.hint: Think about what C translator does with adjacent string literals.
options: Syntax error
explanations: Correct! At Translation Phase 6, adjacent string literals are concatenated by compiler into one: `"Hello World"`. String length is 11 characters + 1 null terminator `\0` = 12 bytes.
Incorrect. 11 is count of printable characters without `\0`.
Incorrect. Compiler concatenates literals, rather than creating an array of two pointers.
Incorrect. Separating strings with spaces or newlines is fully supported by C standards.

questions.topic: Functions — Syntactic Sugar of Array Parameters
questions.q: What will `sizeof(a)` output inside function `void print_size(int a[5][10])` on 64-bit system?
questions.hint: What does ANY top-level array parameter turn into in a C function header?
explanations: Correct! In C function parameters array types do not exist. Declaration `int a[5][10]` implicitly adjusts by compiler to a pointer to its first element: `int (*a)[10]`. Operator `sizeof(a)` returns size of pointer itself (8 bytes on 64-bit system).
Incorrect. $5 \times 10 \times 4 = 200$ bytes would be size of original array outside function parameters.
Incorrect. 40 is size of only one row `int[10]`.
Incorrect. Array size is not implicitly passed within type.

questions.topic: C99 Standards — Scope and Lifetime of Compound Literals
questions.q: Is access `p[0]` to a compound literal outside its block `{}` safe?
questions.hint: What storage duration does a compound literal created inside a block possess?
options: Unsafe (Undefined Behavior): compound literal in a block has automatic storage duration and is destroyed upon exiting `{}`
Safe: compound literal always has static storage duration
Compilation error: forbidden to assign literal to pointer
Safe: prints 1
explanations: Correct! In C99 compound literal declared inside a block `{}` has automatic storage duration bound to that block. Upon exiting block, memory is deallocated and `p` becomes a dangling pointer. Reading `p[0]` is UB.
Incorrect. Only literals declared OUTSIDE all functions (at file scope) have static storage duration.
Incorrect. Assigning address of compound literal to pointer is completely valid inside its block.
Incorrect. Although you may accidentally get 1, code contains a memory bug.

questions.topic: Arrays — Comparing Array Names via == Operator
questions.q: What will condition `if (a == b)` output when comparing two local arrays with identical content?
questions.hint: What do names `a` and `b` represent when participating in binary comparison operations?
options: Prints "Not Equal"
Prints "Equal"
Compilation error
Undefined behavior
explanations: Correct! In C operator `==` does NOT compare array content element-by-element. Names `a` and `b` decay to pointers to their first elements (`&a[0]` and `&b[0]`). Since these are two distinct arrays on stack, their memory addresses differ. Comparison returns 0 (false), printing "Not Equal".
Incorrect. Element-wise array comparison in C is not provided by `==` operator (for strings use `memcmp` or `strcmp`).
Incorrect. Comparing pointers is allowed by language syntax.
Incorrect. Result of comparing two address pointers is clearly defined.
